# Versioning workflow

A workspace per thread, landing finished work, the revision graph, changed-file review, project checks and undo per turn. Works with jj and git.

Pack id `versioning`. Back to [all packs](README.md).

## Plugins

1. [`@dshfiles/jj-integration`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/jj-integration/README.md) — One jj workspace per thread, with a manual integration dashboard and optional Project Checks-verified automatic integration.
2. [`@dshfiles/jujutsu`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/jujutsu/README.md) — Jujutsu revision graph and confirmed Source Control actions for DSH.
3. [`@dshfiles/diff-viewed`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/diff-viewed/README.md) — Mark changed files as viewed in the DSH change review tab, with per-turn progress.
4. [`@dshfiles/session-undo`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/session-undo/README.md) — Undo and redo a thread's last turn: the conversation forks back before it and the workspace files return to their snapshot, through the VCS provider (jj operations in a jj workspace).
5. [`@dshfiles/project-checks`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/project-checks/README.md) — Trusted project actions, completion receipts, and native hook result visibility for DSH.

## Prerequisites

1. A project is added.
2. The project is a jj or git repository.

## Key settings

1. **Isolate each new thread in its own workspace**: Settings entry `jj-integration`, field `isolateByDefault`.
2. **Keep a revision per turn for undo**: Settings entry `dshfiles-session-undo`, field `turnRevisions`.

## Features

From the onboarding feature catalog: 38 features, the 29 curated ones first.

### Curated

1. **New thread destination and workspace isolation** (`jj-integration`, composer) — Choose whether a new thread works in its own workspace or in the project itself.
2. **Thread workspaces in git-only repositories** (`jj-integration`, composer) — Thread workspaces, landing and review history work in a git project without Jujutsu too.
3. **New thread returns to its project** (`jj-integration`, composer) — A new thread returns to its project instead of reusing the last thread's workspace.
4. **New thread prepares its destination while the draft is written** (`jj-integration`, composer) — A new thread's workspace is prepared while you write the draft, so the first send is quick.
5. **Workspace control in the thread header** (`jj-integration`, thread-panel) — The thread header names its workspace and holds Land, the workspaces panel and the thread log download.
6. **Land a thread on its bookmark** (`jj-integration`, thread-panel) — Land a thread's revisions on its bookmark from the header, with a preview of what will land.
7. **Land from the end of a turn** (`jj-integration`, transcript) — The last turn of a thread with its own workspace offers Land right below the answer.
8. **Workspaces page** (`jj-integration`, land) — One page lists every thread workspace by state, and lands every ready one at once.
9. **Workspaces that need you come first** (`jj-integration`, land) — The workspaces page opens on the ones with conflicts, ready work or a block.
10. **Workspace row details** (`jj-integration`, land) — Expand a workspace row to see what blocks it, its revisions, its threads and its path.
11. **No thread workspaces yet** (`jj-integration`, land) — A project without thread workspaces shows one plain sentence instead of empty groups.
12. **Pick a New-thread project** (`jj-integration`, composer) — Pick the project for a new thread, with recent projects first and workspaces listed apart.
13. **Blocked and ready-to-land workspaces in the Inbox** (`jj-integration`, inbox) — A workspace that is ready to land, or blocked, shows in the Inbox with Land or Retry.
14. **Prepare a new thread workspace with trusted setup actions** (`jj-integration`, composer) — Run trusted setup steps when a thread's workspace is created, and optional steps when it is done.
15. **Choose a project's main branch** (`jj-integration`, settings) — Choose the bookmark a project's threads start from and land on, in Settings › Projects.
16. **Stop processes left in a thread workspace before removing it** (`jj-integration`, land) — Processes still running in a workspace are stopped before the workspace is removed.
17. **Locate landmarks and compare revision ancestry** (`jujutsu`, land) — Jump to the working copy, main or main@origin in one click, and compare two revisions when you need to.
18. **Browse and filter the revision graph** (`jujutsu`, land) — Browse the revision graph with bookmarks, workspaces, conflicts and dates, and filter it.
19. **Inspect revisions and changed files** (`jujutsu`, land) — Open a revision's description, files and full diff, and mark files reviewed.
20. **Select revisions in the graph to review them together** (`jujutsu`, land) — Cmd-click or Shift-click revisions in the graph, then review them together.
21. **See a thread's changes in its header** (`jujutsu`, thread-panel) — A thread in its own workspace shows its changed lines in the header, and a click opens Changes.
22. **Preview and confirm repository changes** (`jujutsu`, land) — Squash, rebase, split, abandon and other changes run only after a preview you confirm.
23. **Move a workspace from a shared revision** (`jujutsu`, land) — When several workspaces share a revision, open the overflow chip to see and move them.
24. **Create a workspace at a revision** (`jujutsu`, land) — Right-click a revision and choose New workspace here to create a workspace there.
25. **Open Jujutsu references from a chat message** (`jujutsu`, land) — Revision ids and bookmarks in a message become links that preview a small graph around them.
26. **Clean up idle workspaces** (`jujutsu`, land) — Clean up workspaces idle for an hour, a day or a week, with a preview that protects unlanded work.
27. **Remove a workspace from the graph** (`jujutsu`, land) — Right-click a workspace to remove it, and a thread workspace first names its unlanded revisions.
28. **Describe and review the working copy in Source Control** (`jujutsu`, land) — Describe the working copy and see its changed files and the revisions below it in Source control.
29. **Mark review files as viewed** (`diff-viewed`, thread-panel) — Mark a file as viewed in a review and see how many are left.

### More

1. **Keep one repository per Jujutsu tab** (`jujutsu`) — Each Jujutsu tab, thread and panel keeps its own repository, view, filters and selection.
2. **Keep viewed marks across browsers** (`diff-viewed`) — Viewed marks are kept by DSH, so they stay across browsers and restarts.
3. **One viewed-marks store for turns and revision ranges** (`diff-viewed`) — Viewed marks also work in the Changes tab and the Review page, per revision range.
4. **Undo and redo a turn: conversation and files together** (`session-undo`, composer) — Undo a turn to roll back its conversation and file changes together, and redo it again.
5. **Rewind to before any recorded turn, files included** (`session-undo`, composer) — Rewind to before any turn, files included, from the composer's Rewind menu.
6. **Each turn names the jj revision its edits left, with Restore to here** (`session-undo`, transcript) — Each turn names the revision its edits left, with Restore to here in its menu.
7. **Run trusted project checks** (`project-checks`, composer) — Run trusted project checks, including setup steps for a new workspace, and keep their results.
8. **Show hook runs** (`project-checks`, thread-panel) — See which hooks ran and what they returned.
9. **Project check receipts appear safely in the Activity Timeline** (`project-checks`) — Check results appear in the activity feed, and checks keep working without it.

## Enable it

1. In the app: **Knowledge › Getting started**, then **Enable pack** on Versioning workflow under Packs. It previews exactly what changes; **Disable pack** reverses it.
2. From an Agent: the `onboarding_pack_apply` tool with pack `versioning`. It runs only when you ask, after showing the preview.
3. From a shell: `dshx init --profile <name> --packs versioning` (Core is added; `--dry-run` previews). See [`dshx init`](../../tooling/dshx/docs/cli-reference.md#dshx-init-compose-a-profile-from-packs).

## Restart

Installing a plugin the profile does not have yet needs a DSH Host restart: DSH reads the profile once at boot. Plugins already installed are switched on in the running DSH. Nothing restarts on its own: use **Restart when idle** in the sidebar when DSH runs under the managed launcher, otherwise your own launcher.
